title: Anesthetizing Sea Cucumbers
author: Jon Eilers
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5nyg5fw

steps.title: Prepare menthol stock solution
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 g menthol crystals to 100 mL ethanol in a container and stir or shake until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Make 10 % menthol/ethanol solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the stock solution to a 10 % menthol/ethanol mixture by adding 900 mL salt water to the 100 mL stock, mixing thoroughly.

steps.title: Prepare 40 % working anesthetic
steps.instruction: In a separate container, combine 400 mL of the 10 % menthol/ethanol solution with 600 mL salt water to obtain a 40 % diluted anesthetic solution.

steps.title: Anesthetize sea cucumber
steps.instruction: Place the sea cucumber into the 40 % solution, wait 30 minutes, then gently poke and observe; if unresponsive, the animal is anesthetized; if still responsive, wait an additional 5–10 minutes and poke again. Once anesthetized, remove the animal; it will remain relatively unresponsive for 10–30 minutes, and relaxed feeding tentacles hanging from the mouth confirm anesthesia.

substeps.instruction: Add sea cucumber to the 40 % solution
If still responsive, wait 5–10 minutes and poke again
Remove sea cucumber; note unresponsiveness for 10–30 minutes and relaxed feeding tentacles as indicator
